name: scayle
_readme: SCAYLE as migration target only: a fully managed, headless, API-first commerce engine from ABOUT YOU with a Storefront API, an Admin API, add-on modules and the SCAYLE Panel as back office. There is no inspectable client code base to scan - a project's own code is the frontend it builds on top - so no source role and no as_source block. Seed from the vendor's capability-level material, so API and content details here are best-effort and every one of them must be verified against the client's contract and the current SCAYLE developer documentation.

as_target.default_frontend: SCAYLE Storefront Application (JavaScript/TypeScript reference implementation) deployed on SCAYLE Storefront Hosting - a starting point, not a finished storefront; any framework may be used against the Storefront API

snippets.critic2_persona: senior solution architect who has delivered headless commerce projects on SCAYLE or comparable API-first engines, knows the fashion/lifestyle domain (size and colour matrices, returns, seasonal cycles), and can tell for any requirement whether the core engine covers it, an add-on module covers it, or it becomes frontend or external-service work
snippets.docs_domains: scayle.dev and the SCAYLE developer documentation portal (Storefront API and Admin API references, Storefront Application guides, add-on documentation, webhook catalogue), scayle.com (product, modules, positioning, references). SCAYLE's documentation is reported as still maturing, so expect gaps: where the docs are thin, the authoritative source is the client's contract and SCAYLE solution engineering, and any statement taken from a partner blog must be marked as unverified.
snippets.best_practice: treat the engine as a black box reached only through the Storefront API, the Admin API and webhooks - there is no server-side extension point inside it, so every piece of custom business logic lives in the frontend (BFF layer) or in an external service; keep the frontend's own backend-for-frontend thin and cacheable, since the Storefront API is the performance contract; use the Storefront Application as an accelerator but budget it as a project, not as a shipped storefront; model the variant dimensions (size, colour, fit) with the engine's fashion-oriented product model rather than forcing a foreign schema onto it; drive inbound data (product, price, stock) through the Admin API or the documented bulk import path with idempotent jobs, and consume webhooks for outbound events instead of polling; decide the editorial content system early, because the engine is not a page CMS.
snippets.critic2_focus: D1: which SCAYLE modules and add-ons the client's CONTRACT actually includes - on a modular SaaS, 'standard' means 'contracted', and a documented feature that is not licensed is a gap. D2: is the claimed standard counterpart the core engine, a paid add-on (omni-channel, wholesale), or frontend work in the Storefront Application. D3: does the engine really cover it, or does it land in the frontend or an external service - and for B2B requirements, be explicit that the platform is B2C-focused. D4: exact Storefront API and Admin API resource names and their fields, webhook event names, and any claim that assumes server-side extensibility inside the engine, self-hosting or a built-in page CMS.
snippets.expected_hotspots_d3: check rather than assume: B2B in every form - the platform ships a basic wholesale module and customer-group pricing, while approvals, budgets, organisation hierarchies, quotes, punchout and contract pricing are absent, and complex B2B is a poor fit; editorial content, landing pages and campaign pages (no page CMS in the engine - see content_model_notes); non-fashion product data models and PIM-grade attribute governance, workflows and data quality rules; deep tax and legal country matrices beyond the supported markets; subscriptions and recurring orders; marketplace or multi-vendor scenarios; configurable, bundled or made-to-order products; live ERP pricing and availability inside the shopper request; returns and RMA depth beyond the fashion returns flow; loyalty programmes; customer service tooling beyond the Panel; anything requiring server-side custom logic inside the commerce engine.
snippets.expected_blockers_d4: check before committing: SaaS with no self-hosting and no code deployed into the engine - extensibility is the API surface, webhooks and the add-on catalogue, so any requirement needing logic inside the commerce core becomes an external service and a new system in the landscape; the frontend must be built AND operated (Storefront Hosting reduces the DevOps burden but the storefront is still project scope); no shipped page CMS, so an external headless CMS is usually added, which brings a second content model, a second editorial workflow and a rendering contract to design; the module and add-on model means 'standard' depends on the commercial package - verify each feature against the contract, not the documentation; young ecosystem with fewer SI partners and add-ons than established platforms, so partner availability and reference checks are a real project risk; documentation maturity, which slows estimation and integration design; B2B gaps as listed in expected_hotspots_d3; geographic reach strongest in DACH and Europe, so non-European market, tax and payment requirements need explicit confirmation; API rate limits, bulk import throughput and webhook delivery guarantees must be obtained in writing before an integration is designed.
snippets.content_model_notes: SCAYLE is a commerce engine, not a content platform, and no CMS module is listed - the vendor material names product information management, media management, internationalisation and the Panel as back office, with nothing about pages, layouts or components. Treat that as the working assumption *(verify whether a SCAYLE CMS or content module exists in the client's contract)*. Consequence for the content model: the content SCAYLE owns is entity-bound - product and variant attributes, product media sets, category and brand content, filter labels, promotion and campaign presentation, SEO metadata per entity, store profiles from the omni-channel add-on. Editorial content that is NOT entity-bound - landing pages, campaign pages, editorial storytelling, navigation copy, legal pages - has no home in the engine and comes either from the storefront application's own code or from an external headless CMS, which is the common pattern for this platform class. So estimate two content models, not one, and put the page composition, the component library and the editor experience into the frontend/CMS scope rather than the platform scope. 'content block' as the term in deliverables therefore usually means a block in the chosen external CMS, not a SCAYLE object.
snippets.api_families_hint: see knowledge target_api_endpoint_families - Storefront API (shopper-facing, REST and GraphQL options) and Admin API (management), plus an Add-on API for extended modules; resource names are best-effort and must be verified against the current API reference
